To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose and evaluate a hybrid model to predict popularity and understand the underlying mechanisms, and we develop a novel RNN architecture that connects heterogeneous streams to model and predict online attention.

(1) we bridge gaps between feature and generative models by introducing a hybrid model, and propose a benchmark for popularity prediction, (2) we propose a novel model that links multiple heterogeneous sources of external influences to predict popularity of online content in a unified framework.
(1) we develop and connect models for popularity prediction in social media across different paradiggs and settings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the popularity of information in online social networks.
developing and linking models across feature driven, and process driven approaches to predict and understand online attention and popularity.
understanding and predicting the online popularity of content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this thesis has contributed to the field of social media analysis in two major ways. Firstly, it connects and compares different paradigms of online popularity modeling and prediction.
we have developed a new hybrid model and a benchmark to connect and compare models for online popularity prediction.

this dissertation has contributed to the literature on popularity prediction and modeling by proposing new hybrid models that link models across paradigms, and by introducing a benchmark for popularity prediction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thesis contributes to a better understanding and prediction of online popularity by linking models across paradigms and sources of influence.

we have developed a novel hybrid model to predict and understand the popularity of online content, and we have connected multiple sources of information in the form of asynchronous streams for modeling the collective attention in social media.

we developed new models and benchmarks for popularity prediction and understanding, and we connected models from feature-driven and generative paradigns to predict and understand the popularity of online content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can connect and compare models across different paradigns.
a generative model can be used to predict popularity, but it requires careful design of the generative process to achieve good performance.
the generative and feature driven paradigms are complementary and that a hybrid model is a good way to connect them.
